Title: Pre-pour slab inspection
L1 Factual Knowledge: A pre-pour inspection checks important construction work before concrete placement makes that work difficult or impossible to inspect.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: The relevant work is inspected before the concrete pour and any identified issues are addressed before proceeding.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The required checks depend on the work present at the stage and the applicable project requirements.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner looks for work that will become concealed by the concrete and therefore needs to be checked before the pour.
L5 Context and Dependencies: This activity depends on relevant pre-pour work being complete and occurs before concrete placement.

Title: Temporary wall frame bracing
L1 Factual Knowledge: Temporary bracing supports a wall frame while the structure is not yet fully stabilised by later construction work.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: Bracing is installed as part of the framing sequence and remains in place while temporary stability is required.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The need and arrangement of temporary bracing depend on the frame condition and construction sequence.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner considers whether the partially completed frame can remain stable while subsequent work is carried out.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Temporary bracing is connected to the wall framing sequence and later stability of the structure.

Title: Wall frame inspection before concealment
L1 Factual Knowledge: Wall framing should be inspected at an appropriate stage before later construction work conceals relevant parts of the frame.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: The frame is reviewed before subsequent lining or other work makes the relevant construction difficult to inspect.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The timing of the inspection depends on when the relevant framing work will become concealed.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner pays particular attention to items that will no longer be visible after the next construction stage.
L5 Context and Dependencies: The inspection depends on completion of the relevant framing work and precedes work that conceals the frame.

Title: Roof framing set-out
L1 Factual Knowledge: Roof framing set-out establishes the intended positions of roof framing elements before installation proceeds.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: Relevant positions are established and checked as part of the roof framing sequence before the associated members are installed.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The set-out depends on the roof configuration and the information applicable to the construction.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner checks whether the set-out is consistent before errors are repeated across later roof framing work.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Roof framing set-out follows relevant supporting construction and informs subsequent roof framing installation.

Title: Under-slab drainage inspection
L1 Factual Knowledge: Under-slab drainage includes drainage work that will become difficult to access after the slab is constructed.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: The relevant drainage work is checked before it becomes concealed by subsequent slab construction.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The checks depend on the drainage work present and the stage at which it will become inaccessible.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner focuses on work that cannot be easily corrected once concrete has been placed.
L5 Context and Dependencies: The inspection occurs after the relevant drainage work is installed and before slab construction conceals it.

Title: Wet-area wall framing consideration
L1 Factual Knowledge: Wall framing in a wet-area context may have requirements influenced by the construction and finishes associated with that area.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: The framing arrangement is checked against the relevant design and construction requirements before later finishes are installed.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The appropriate framing arrangement can change depending on the wall system, finishes and project requirements.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner considers how later wet-area construction will interact with the framing rather than treating the frame in isolation.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Wet-area framing decisions connect framing work with later lining, waterproofing and finishing activities.

Title: Construction sequencing and concealment
L1 Factual Knowledge: Construction sequencing determines the order in which related activities are carried out.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: Work is planned so that required inspections and checks occur before later activities conceal or restrict access to earlier work.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The sequence can change when dependencies, access requirements or construction conditions change.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner looks ahead to identify work that will become inaccessible if the next activity proceeds.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Sequencing connects preceding work, inspections, concealment points and downstream construction activities.

Title: Wall frame set-out
L1 Factual Knowledge: Wall frame set-out establishes the intended position of wall framing before the frame is completed.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: Wall positions are established from the relevant project information and checked before framing proceeds.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: Set-out decisions depend on the building layout and information applicable to the particular wall.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner checks the relationship between the wall position and surrounding construction before errors become difficult to correct.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Wall frame set-out depends on earlier building layout information and informs subsequent framing activities.

Title: Evidence before work is concealed
L1 Factual Knowledge: Evidence of completed work provides a record that relevant construction was checked before it became concealed.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: Required evidence is captured at the appropriate stage before subsequent construction prevents normal observation of the work.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The evidence required depends on the activity, inspection requirements and the type of work being concealed.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner recognises the last practical opportunity to inspect or record work before access is lost.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Evidence collection is linked to inspection, concealment points and later verification of completed construction.

Title: Construction decision dependencies
L1 Factual Knowledge: A construction decision can depend on earlier work, available information and other related decisions.
L2 Procedural Knowledge: Dependencies are identified before making a decision so that relevant preceding conditions and downstream effects can be considered.
L3 Conditional Knowledge: The importance of a dependency changes according to the construction context and the decision being made.
L4 Expert Judgement: An experienced practitioner considers not only the immediate decision but also what has to happen before it and what it will affect afterwards.
L5 Context and Dependencies: Decision dependencies connect related Knowledge Objects through preceding, following and dependency relationships.
